advisory.summary: out-of-bounds read panic in language.Parse on a malformed BCP-47 tag

acquisition.notes: Liveness-augmented counterpart of the GO-2021-0113 trivial repro: the same parseHandler route (GET / on 127.0.0.1:8080) pins the VULNERABLE golang.org/x/text v0.3.6 and passes the untrusted Accept-Language header straight into language.Parse inside a defer/recover. Adds a marker-gated benign liveness beacon (X-Tegron-Liveness) on the success path that the exploit trace never sends, so a patched-build detonation stays dark. Vendored with go.mod + vendor/ so the Go toolchain builds it hermetically.

expected_verdict.label: reasoned_exploitable
expected_verdict.rationale: language.Parse (the GO-2021-0113 out-of-bounds-read sink) is reached directly from the HTTP handler on the affected x/text v0.3.6, so the ingress-to-sink taint path is statically complete and the row is reachable. Live confirmation of the panic requires a malformed BCP-47 tag delivered against a vulnerable-toolchain build under a controlled sandbox, so analysis stops at reachable-but-unconfirmed (stopped_capability); the verdict is reasoned, not proven -- the repro carries no proven live-canary flag. KnownGap: this row is surfaced in the corpus but not yet measured end-to-end -- until PLAN-020's per-language dispatch and this lane's populated symbol lists and ground truth land, the fixture Loads and Validates cleanly but the stub pipeline emits a uniform verdict, so direction/strength equality is not asserted (assertable_now=false), mirroring the symboltest harness's documented gap.
